A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RIGVid study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–K. The material supports reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original physical-robot experiments, video-filtering measurements and baseline comparisons in Section 4, with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original robot evaluations, filtering measurements, baseline comparisons and appendix experiments. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged.

M1.justification: The video-generation, VLM-filtering, depth-estimation, 6D tracking, grasping, retargeting and closed-loop execution procedures are unchanged. The mesh-free variant and trajectory smoothing were already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate pouring, lid lifting, spatula placement and sweeping, alongside the same additional manipulation tasks and ALOHA/bimanual demonstrations. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: ReKep, Track2Act, AVDC, 4D-DPM and Gen2Act remain the evaluated main comparators, with the same appendix tracking comparisons. The newly cited related work is not added as an experimental baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain fixed initial configurations, shared videos across baselines, human-judged success criteria and 10 videos per task/source. The appendix video-quality and trajectory-jitter evaluation protocols also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The filtering comparisons, mesh-free test, ReKep failure cases, point-tracking limitations, perturbation examples, depth ablation and MegaPose/FoundationPose jitter analysis are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Trial counts, averaging practices and Pearson correlation reporting are unchanged. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty estimates are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. Both report 85% RIGVid success versus 50% for ReKep in Figure 8 and 67.5% for Gen2Act in Figure 9. Tables 1 and 3 and the appendix results also retain their values.

T1.justification: The fixed object-to-end-effector transformation assumption and Appendix J's translational and rotational RMS-jitter definitions are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning, formal results or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about manipulation without physical demonstrations, filtered generated videos matching real-video supervision, and advantages over VLM-based and alternative trajectory-extraction methods.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of depth-related failures and tracking advantages under occlusion and rotation. Qualifications concerning ReKep, mesh requirements, slow mesh-free tracking and video-generation cost are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware descriptions, prompts, filtering settings, recovery thresholds, smoothing instructions, baseline adaptations and runtime disclosures remain unchanged. The project URL is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al. (2024), One-shot video imitation via parameterized symbolic abstraction graphs, as reference 115 in Section 2's Direct Imitation from Videos citation list. Existing references are renumbered; the substantive positioning and novelty discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes Unnat Jain's Skild AI affiliation, renumbers Columbia's affiliation, and adds Shikhar Bahl to the acknowledgements, with a small wording edit there. Scientific prose and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: All 21 figures and three tables retain their content, design and placement. The added reference causes limited bibliography reflow on pages 15–16, with minor text wrapping and affiliation-layout changes elsewhere.

improvement.justification: v3 adds one related-work citation and updates affiliation and acknowledgement text, but leaves the method, empirical evidence, claims, limitations and reproducibility information unchanged, including the appendices. These limited attribution and editorial updates do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall scientific support or clarity.
